title: A median minimizes the L¹ deviation c ↦ ∫|u − c| on a probability space
statement: Let X be a measurable space (X : Type), μ a probability measure on X, u : X → ℝ μ-integrable, and β ∈ ℝ a median of u: μ{x : β ≤ u(x)} ≥ 1/2 and μ{x : u(x) ≤ β} ≥ 1/2, where μ(A) := μ.real A = (μ A).toReal and 1/2 is the real one half. Then ∫_X |u − β| dμ ≤ ∫_X |u − c| dμ for every c ∈ ℝ.
lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (μ : Measure X) (u : X → ℝ) (β : ℝ), IsProbabilityMeasure μ → Integrable u μ → 1 / 2 ≤ μ.real {x | β ≤ u x} → 1 / 2 ≤ μ.real {x | u x ≤ β} → ∀ c : ℝ, ∫ x, |u x - β| ∂μ ≤ ∫ x, |u x - c| ∂μ
